subject: Retroactive coverage question & bridge letter request for hosting modes
messages:
From: Rachel O'Neil <rachel.oneil@horizondata.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@horizondata.com, security@horizondatasec.com
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 Type II — coverage for Dedicated pools / VPC (audit window question)

Hi Lauren,

Thanks for taking this. We're in the final stages of Horizon Data's procurement cycle and have two quick questions around Redwood's SOC 2 Type II evidence:

1) Does your current SOC 2 Type II report (latest period appears to be 2026-07-01 to 2027-01-31) cover requests served from Redwood Dedicated reserved pools and Private/VPC/on-prem deployments, or is it limited to the hosted/shared API?

2) We have a tight compliance deadline — we need formal attestation that controls were in place for the period Feb 1, 2027 — Apr 30, 2027. If Redwood's formal report does not explicitly list Dedicated/VPC, would Redwood issue a bridge letter attesting that the same control set covered particular Dedicated pools and the customer VPC for that window? Is it possible to have the bridge letter reference retroactive evidence (config snapshots, tenancy IDs, change logs) to extend coverage for that period?

We need any formal language and an estimated turnaround for internal reviewers by Jun 10. Happy to jump on a short call if that's easier.

Thanks,
Rachel
Director, IT Security | Horizon Data
security@horizondatasec.com
Attachment: procurement_requirements_2027Q2.pdf (pdf)

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com>

Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II — coverage for Dedicated pools / VPC (audit window question)

Hi Rachel — thanks for the clear ask and timeline.

Short answer up front: our published SOC 2 Type II report covers the hosted API endpoints by default. Dedicated pools and Private/VPC/on-prem are not automatically included unless they were explicitly in-scope for the audit or we produce a scoped bridge letter with supporting evidence.

I'll loop in Security (Neha) and our Legal/Compliance contacts to confirm feasibility for your requested window (Feb 1 — Apr 30, 2027) and what evidence we'd need to substantiate retroactive coverage.

Next steps from our side:
- Neha: can you confirm whether the customer's dedicated pool tenancy IDs and our config snapshots exist for Feb–Apr?
- Legal/Compliance: we will need to draft bridge language and confirm sign-off timelines.
- Rachel: can you share the exact tenant IDs or the HubSpot deal ID so we can map logs and change history?

I expect a firm answer and draft bridge-letter by Jun 4 if we have the tenant IDs and evidence. If not, I'll come back with the earliest possible ETA.

Cheers,
Lauren Bishop

Date: Thu, 3 Jun 2027 08:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II — coverage for Dedicated pools / VPC (audit window question)

Lauren / team — quick technical/compliance summary from Security:

1) Baseline: the SOC 2 Type II report we circulated (period 2026-07-01 to 2027-01-31) was scoped to Redwood-hosted control environment and shared runtime endpoints. That report does not list per-customer dedicated pools or customer-managed VPCs as in-scope entities.

2) Dedicated pools: we can include dedicated reserved pools in a bridge letter provided we can produce authoritative evidence that the same controls were implemented for those pools during the requested window. Typical evidence we require:
  - tenancy IDs or pool identifiers (explicit list)
  - infrastructure config snapshots (firewall/NACLs, IAM roles) for the targeted dates
  - change logs / deployment manifests showing no control deviations during the window
  - monitoring/alerting records and patching snapshots

3) Private/VPC/on-prem: these are treated case-by-case. For customer-managed VPCs or on-prem deployments we can provide a statement of controls we operate (where applicable) and request customer-supplied evidence for their side of the controls. Bridge letters can reference hybrid responsibilities but cannot retroactively assert control over customer-managed infrastructure unless we have corroborating evidence.

4) Retroactive coverage: SOC auditors generally do not re-issue past opinions; however, a bridge letter can state that controls were in place during the period if the supporting artifacts exist and have been validated by our compliance team. Legal will want strongly circumscribed language ("to the best of our knowledge based on provided artifacts") and we will not certify auditor opinion retroactively.

5) Time & deliverables: assuming Horizon can provide pool IDs + requested artifacts by EOD Jun 3, Security + Compliance can produce a bridge-letter draft by Jun 6 for legal review. Legal approval + sign-off typically takes 48–72 hours thereafter.

Attached: bridge-letter-draft-20270603.docx (draft, internal) and an evidence checklist spreadsheet.

Neha Kapoor
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II — coverage for Dedicated pools / VPC (audit window question)

Hi Rachel — quick update and next steps.

Thanks for the prompt follow-up and for sending the HubSpot ID in your last note (HubSpot:HS1234567). We reviewed internally: Security confirms we can prepare a bridge letter that references the control set and the specific dedicated pool IDs you provided earlier. A few important notes:

- Draft and scope: we'll produce a concise bridge letter that describes the controls Redwood operated for the named dedicated pools and, where applicable, the perimeter controls we manage for Private/VPC deployments. The draft will include an evidence appendix listing the tenancy IDs and artifact types we validated.
- Retroactive language: Legal requires the bridge to be explicit that it is not an auditor re-issue of the SOC 2 opinion — rather, it attests that, based on reviewed artifacts, controls were present during Feb 1 — Apr 30, 2027.
- Timeline: Security will deliver a first draft by EOD Jun 6. Legal review and signatures typically complete within 48–72 hours after that. We can route the final letter via DocuSign.
- Evidence needed from Horizon: tenancy/pool IDs, exported firewall/NACL snapshots for the Feb–Apr window, any customer-side configuration that affects control ownership. Please upload artifacts to the secure SFTP link in the HubSpot record or share a protected Drive link.

I'll attach the draft bridge letter and the SOC 2 Type II PDF we referenced for your reviewers to begin their internal check. If you need language stronger than "based on reviewed artifacts," we will need to coordinate with our external auditor which will add time.

Next: Rachel — if you can confirm receipt of the draft and upload the artifacts by Jun 5, we'll aim to get final signed letter to you by Jun 9.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwoodinference.com
